root_cause.text: The virtio_bt driver failed to validate that the remaining skb payload contains at least the minimum fixed HCI header size for each packet type before passing it to hci_recv_frame(), allowing out-of-bounds reads when processing truncated packets from an untrusted backend.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds per-packet-type minimum header size validation (HCI_EVENT_PKT requires 2 bytes, HCI_ACLDATA_PKT requires 4 bytes, etc.) and checks `if (skb->len < min_hdr)` before calling `hci_recv_frame()`. The CVE description explicitly states that "none of the switch cases in virtbt_rx_handle() check skb->len against the per-type minimum HCI header size before handing the frame to the core," and demonstrates the concrete hazard: a one-byte HCI_ACLDATA_PKT packet causes `hci_acl_hdr(skb)->handle` to dereference uninitialized buffer data when the HCI device has active CIS/BIS/PA connections.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce a new local variable `min_hdr` to support packet header size validation logic in the Bluetooth virtio device receive handler.
intent_record.what: Added a new local variable declaration `size_t min_hdr;` at the beginning of the `virtbt_rx_handle` function, before the existing `__u8 pkt_type;` declaration.
intent_record.how: This change introduces a new variable into the function's scope that can be used in subsequent logic (not shown in this hunk). The variable is sized as `size_t` to hold a minimum header size value, likely for bounds checking or validation of incoming Bluetooth packets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add packet length validation to prevent processing of malformed Bluetooth HCI packets with insufficient header data.
intent_record.what: Refactored the switch statement to extract packet type handling into a min_hdr size assignment pattern, moved hci_skb_pkt_type() and hci_recv_frame() calls outside the switch block, added a new length validation check comparing skb->len against min_hdr with error logging, and changed the default case from break to return.
intent_record.how: The code now validates that incoming socket buffers have sufficient length for their packet type's header structure before processing. Previously, packets were processed without length validation, which could cause buffer overread or underflow. The validation occurs after type classification but before frame reception, preventing malformed packets from reaching the HCI layer. The default case now returns early instead of breaking, avoiding potential null/invalid pointer dereference if min_hdr was uninitialized.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the `virtbt_rx_handle()` function (lines 177-192). The function extracts the packet type from the first byte of the skb without validating that the skb contains sufficient data for the HCI header. Specifically: (1) Line 179 reads `pkt_type = *((__u8 *) skb->data)` without checking if skb->len >= 1, (2) Line 180 calls `skb_pull(skb, 1)` which reduces the payload, and (3) Line 186 calls `hci_recv_frame(vbt->hdev, skb)` without validating that the remaining payload meets the minimum HCI header size requirements for each packet type (HCI_EVENT_PKT requires at least 2 bytes for event code and parameter length, HCI_ACLDATA_PKT requires at least 4 bytes, HCI_SCODATA_PKT requires at least 3 bytes, HCI_ISODATA_PKT requires at least 4 bytes). When processing truncated packets from an untrusted backend, this allows out-of-bounds reads in hci_recv_frame(). The code lacks any length validation before passing the skb to hci_recv_frame().

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the `virtbt_rx_handle()` function (lines 189-203). The function extracts the packet type from the first byte of the skb without validating that the skb contains sufficient data for the HCI header. Specifically: (1) Line 191 reads `pkt_type = *((__u8 *) skb->data)` without checking if skb->len >= 1, (2) Line 192 calls `skb_pull(skb, 1)` unconditionally, and (3) Line 197 calls `hci_recv_frame(vbt->hdev, skb)` without validating that the remaining payload contains the minimum HCI header size for each packet type (HCI_EVENT_PKT requires at least 2 bytes for event code and parameter length, HCI_ACLDATA_PKT requires at least 4 bytes for handle and length, etc.). The `virtbt_rx_work()` function at line 207 sets `skb->len = len` from the virtqueue but never validates this length is sufficient before calling `virtbt_rx_handle()`. An untrusted backend can send truncated packets that will cause out-of-bounds reads when `hci_recv_frame()` processes them.
